newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA sees July 1 deadline for Phoenix RFG plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA sees July 1 deadline for Phoenix RFG plan.

text.p: Federal regulators, reaffirming their plans to help cut smog in Phoenix, Arizona, said Friday they hope to require West Coast oil refiners to sell cleaner burning gasoline there from July 1.

Still, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) cannot set an official start date until Phoenix residents finish getting their say in a federally-required 30-day public comment period that ends this month.
The review allows critics of the new reformulated gasoline (RFG) plan to state their concerns. No more hearings are scheduled but the public can file written comments with EPA.
"The manufacturers need to be preparing to provide RFG to Arizona this summer because its inevitable," EPA's Wittorp said.

On Friday, EPA let expire its option to mandate the program without public hearing. That option, known as a "direct final rule," was considered defunct as soon as Chevron requested a delay of the program last month, industry sources said.

Phoenix, like a handful of U.S. cities and states, has volunteered to require RFG as part of a plan to improve air quality, particularly smog, which has grown in severity in Phoenix and its burgeoning suburbs in recent years.
The Phoenix area has fallen out of compliance with national clean air standards in recent years, with smog levels exceeding federal limits several days out of the year.
Around 30 percent of gasoline sold in the U.S. is RFG and 30 billion gallons of it has replaced conventional gasoline since the 1990 Clean Air Act required it, industry sources said.
